tagline: Japan's textbook island mesh — a dense hub-and-spoke ferry grid out of Ishigaki serving a UNESCO wilderness, all on exposed-water diesel.
summary: The Yaeyama group is Japan's southernmost archipelago and its purest captive island-mesh market: Ishigaki is the hub, with Taketomi (~3.5 nm), Kohama (~10 nm), Iriomote (~15 nm), Kuroshima and Hateruma radiating out on a high-frequency ferry grid run by a two-operator duopoly. Iriomote is a UNESCO Natural World Heritage wilderness with a hard 1,200-visitors-a-day cap; the water between the islands is shallow, reef-fringed and some of the clearest in Asia. Every leg sits inside all-electric range — the geometry of the Maldives playbook, transplanted to Japan.

demand_signals.label: Hub-ferry frequency
demand_signals.value: Up to ~10 daily Ishigaki ↔ Taketomi sailings
demand_signals.note: Anei Kankou and Yaeyama Kanko Ferry run a dense duopoly grid from Ishigaki's Yaeyama terminal to Taketomi, Iriomote (Ohara/Uehara), Kohama, Kuroshima and Hateruma — a proven, captive, high-frequency island-hopping market.
demand_signals.source: Anei Kankou / Yaeyama Kanko Ferry timetables

demand_signals.label: UNESCO wilderness with a visitor cap
demand_signals.note: Iriomote (UNESCO Natural World Heritage, 2021) now operates under a tourism-management plan limiting daily visitors — quality-over-volume access where clean, quiet, low-wake arrival is the conservation-aligned standard.
demand_signals.source: Taketomi Town tourism management plan / Travel Voice, 2023

demand_signals.label: Exposed-water cancellations
demand_signals.value: Hateruma route cancelled routinely in NE monsoon
demand_signals.note: The outer crossings (especially Ohara ↔ Hateruma) are notoriously rough and cancellation-prone — Hateruma is famous for being hard to reach. Weather-fragility is the single strongest reliability hook in the group.
demand_signals.source: Anei Kankou operating practice (reservation-required outer routes)

demand_signals.label: Prefecture-scale demand
demand_signals.note: Ishigaki and the Yaeyamas are the prefecture's flagship dive-and-wilderness destination, with direct mainland flights into Ishigaki's new airport feeding the ferry hub.

use_cases.title: All-electric Yaeyama mesh
use_cases.body: Replace diesel on the hub-and-spoke grid: Ishigaki ↔ Taketomi (~3.5 nm), Kohama (~10 nm), Iriomote (~15 nm), Kuroshima (~10 nm) — short, dense, reef-fringed hops that are the cleanest possible fit for a zero-emission foiling fleet, with shallow-draft access to village jetties.

use_cases.title: Scheduled inter-island service at N35 capacity
use_cases.body: The duopoly's high-frequency scheduled flows (10+ daily sailings on trunk legs) map onto a 12–15-pax scheduled foiling shuttle tier — keeping the timetable the islands depend on while cutting noise, wake and emissions in protected water.

use_cases.title: Resort-jetty island-hopping
use_cases.body: Direct foiling transfers across the hotel set — ANA InterContinental Ishigaki, Club Med Kabira, Hoshinoya Taketomi, Haimurubushi Kohama, Hoshino's Iriomote hotel — turning the ferry-plus-shuttle chain into one premium hop.

use_cases.title: Cross-archipelago line-hauls
use_cases.body: Miyako ↔ Ishigaki (~70–80 nm by sea) and Naha ↔ Ishigaki (~220 nm) are air-only today — Quanta-LR hybrid line-hauls link the Yaeyamas to the rest of the prefecture with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

journeys.today: An open-water diesel ferry that gets rough on exposed days and is cancelled outright in heavy weather, stranding day-trippers to the UNESCO wilderness.
journeys.with_navier: A smooth, near-silent foiling crossing that flies above the chop and arrives in World Heritage water clean and quiet — matched to the island's 1,200-a-day visitor cap.

journeys.today: The group's densest shuttle — up to ~10 diesel round trips a day to a heritage village island a few nautical miles away.
journeys.with_navier: A zero-emission, low-wake shuttle on the trunk leg — same frequency, none of the diesel, in water this clear.

journeys.today: The group's most exposed leg, reservation-gated and frequently cancelled — Hateruma's inaccessibility is legendary.
journeys.with_navier: Foiling above the swell widens the operable window on the crossing that defeats conventional hulls most often.

journeys.today: Air-only — no passenger surface link between the prefecture's two southern island groups.
journeys.with_navier: A ~70–80 nm hybrid foiling line-haul stitches Miyako and the Yaeyamas into one network — just past all-electric range, natural Quanta-LR territory.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The entire intra-Yaeyama mesh sits deep inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope: Taketomi ~3.5 nm, Kohama ~10 nm, Kuroshima ~10 nm, Iriomote ~15 nm, Hateruma ~26–30 nm from Ishigaki (~15 nm from Ohara). Shallow reef-fringed water rewards shallow-draft foiling; the value is reliability, silence and zero emissions in protected water.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Cross-archipelago legs are explicitly hybrid: Miyako ↔ Ishigaki (~70–80 nm by sea — just past the electric edge) and Naha ↔ Ishigaki (~220 nm). These are air-only today; Quanta-LR adds the surface spine without grid dependency on the outer islands. Never imply one continuous all-electric network across the clusters.

competitive_landscape: A two-operator duopoly — Anei Kankou and Yaeyama Kanko Ferry — runs the dense diesel grid from Ishigaki, with up to ~10 daily sailings on the Taketomi trunk and reservation-gated service to Hateruma. The frequency and load factors prove a mature, captive island-hopping market; the pain is exposure (rough, cancellation-prone outer legs), diesel emissions and wake in some of Japan's clearest reef water, and zero premium or on-demand tier. Between archipelagos, Ryukyu Air Commuter and JTA carry everything by air. The incumbents' volume is the demand evidence; their fleet is the upgrade opportunity.

precedents.why_it_matters: The Yaeyamas are Japan's closest analogue to the Maldives geometry — a captive hub-and-spoke island mesh entirely inside electric range, plus a long hybrid spine to the capital island. The playbook transplants directly.

seasonality: Typhoon season (Jun–Oct) and the NE winter monsoon (Nov–Mar) define the cancellation calendar — the inner lagoon legs stay relatively sheltered (<1 m) while the outer reef-pass and Hateruma crossings see 1.5–2.5 m and frequent suspensions. Foiling above the sea state converts the group's weather-fragility into a reliability premium precisely when conventional ferries stop. Late spring and early autumn between the windows are the calm diving peaks.
regulatory_note: Operations sit under the Japan Coast Guard 11th Regional HQ and MLIT Kyushu, with pier jurisdiction at Ishigaki Port and Taketomi Town's island jetties. Iriomote's UNESCO inscription (2021) plus the Iriomote-Ishigaki National Park bring a hard conservation framework — including the 1,200-visitor daily cap and wake/noise sensitivity in the Iriomote wildcat habitat — that makes zero-emission, low-wake, quiet operation a permitting advantage, not just a brand position. Aligns with Japan's 2050 carbon-neutrality target and MLIT zero-emission-vessel programmes.
